cleanneurons Part G (loop neurons zeroed, generation), Olmo 3 base, cue, MATH-500 n=500, T 0.6 / top-p 1.0, seed 1,000,000, grader v3, paired with the unedited cell (378 right, 98 cap hits, 71 rule-A loops, 4,690 tokens/problem; reproduces result-dadeec to the token). Zeroing the down_proj columns of 1,000 MLP neurons (0.28 %) ranked on 14 real loops by attribution: loops 71 -> 19, cap hits 98 -> 39, tokens/problem 3,870 (-17 %), right 381 (+0.6 points [-3.4, 4.6]). 100 neurons ranked by activation: loops 47, cap 68, tokens 4,246, right 393 (+3.0 [-0.8, 6.6]). Control, 1,000 random neurons: loops 74, cap 104, right 370 (-1.6 [-5.4, 2.2]). So loops in this base are driven by a small, specific neuron set (random neurons do nothing), and removing them saves tokens without a detectable accuracy gain: a removed loop is one more draw at a hard problem (of the 71 looped problems, 33 right with the edit, 25 with random neurons). No row beats the 415 bar. Also: Goodfire's top-K activation mask at 860 of 11,008 raises normal-text loss 36.9 % here (2.9 % reported on Qwen3.6-35B-A3B); at 3,300 it is 3.2 %. Second read of grader v3 (idea-884e91, the DIRECTION open item): every v1/v3 disagreement in the 4,178 Day-1 #3 rows (MATH-500, base+cue job -153825-208b and RL job -183640-e828) read by a second model. 96 disagreements: base 77 wrong-to-right and 1 right-to-wrong, RL 18 wrong-to-right. 42 are the gold string after removing spaces, dollar signs and degree marks; the other 54 read by hand: 0 wrong answers accepted. Causes: unicode root and power signs, vectors written as tuples against a pmatrix gold, two boxes for a two-value gold, **Answer** forms. 2 lenient: '2516' and '4343' accepted for '2516_8' and '4343_6' (base problems 71, 338; the text names the base). The one right-to-wrong (base problem 39 sample 1, answer 23) is v3's error, against the base. So v3's +21 for the base and +5 for RL over v1 is format, not leniency. These are other rows than the 113 flips of rln4_grader_v3.py (raw answers in S3, not read here). Rows in runs/ (not committed).

RL's gain on MATH-500 is mostly a reliability shift: 81% of the 198-sample gap (4 samples per problem, n=500, T 1.0, v3; base+cue 1,642 right of 2,000, RL 1,840) sits in problems the base solves at least once in 4; 19% [11, 27] in problems with base 0 of 4. Cell base 3/4 -> RL 4/4: 86 problems = 43% of the gap. Held-out check (class by 3 base samples, score the 4th): the class 'other three wrong' holds 14% [5, 23] of the gap and the base still solves 15% there; in the class 'other three right' the base fails 7.2%, RL 0.9% (43% of the gap). Homogeneous binomial null predicts 0.5 problems at 0/4, observed 33. Only 2 problems go from 0/4 to 4/4 (170, 279); of the 33 base-0/4 problems RL has 0/4 on 16. Level 5 holds 44% [35, 54] of the gap (27% of problems); Intermediate Algebra 30% [22, 39] (19%). Base wrong samples: 250 finished-wrong, 89 cap hits, 19 no answer; RL is right on the same problems 68%, 49%, 83%. Blind judge (Claude subagents with a fixed rubric; no hosted provider key works on this machine) on 60 base / 30 RL finished-wrong: base slip 35% [24, 48], wrong plan 28%, misread 23%, format 13%; RL slip 17%, wrong plan 67%, misread 17%, format 0. Two passes agree on 44 of 45, kappa 0.97 (same model). Controls: shuffled pairs 15/15 mismatch; planted slips 11/15 and 13/15 (misses all labeled format: slip vs format is unreliable for an error in the last line). Base items with a right sibling: 39 of 48 slip/misread/format; without (base 0/4): 8 of 12 wrong plan. About 52 of the base's 358 wrong samples (36 to 79) fail in stating the answer (placeholder left, form rejected by v3, no answer); RL 0. First wrong step at median 0.20 of the answer. Temperature hybrid, simulated from stored rows (MATH-500, base+cue, v3, no GPU): sample at T 0.6/top-p 1.0 (job -151718-d4fa: 378 right, 98 cap hits; 378 of its 402 finished answers are right, 94 %), and resample only the 98 cap hits once at T 1.0 (the four samples of job -153825-208b). Right of 500: 422, 424, 427, 432 (mean 426.2) at 6,442 tokens per problem, 5,138 if the T 0.6 attempt stops when loop rule A fires (it flags 70 of the 98 cap hits, 1 of 402 finished). References: T 1.0 single 405-418 (mean 410.5, 4,008 tokens), T 1.0 with up to 2 restarts 413-425 (mean 418, 4,924 tokens). So +3.1 points over one T 1.0 sample and +1.7 over T 1.0 restart; paired intervals include 0 in 10 of 12 sample pairings, and the T 0.6 side is one run. Cause: on the 402 problems that finish at T 0.6, T 1.0 gets 361-364 against 378. Not run on GPU: the gain is under 2 points against the equal-effort baseline. Free for anyone: four T 0.6 samples to test a vote of hybrid chains.

xreward Part 1 (weights only, 224 layer matrices, top-8 singular subspaces of model minus base; job abaybektursun-1114-220151-daaa): RL runs with different rewards do NOT write one shared subspace. Input-side (right vectors) overlap, random subspace 0.002: Math 3.0 with Math 3.1 0.476; Code 3.0 with Code 3.1 0.425; Math with Code 0.22-0.26; IF with General 0.187; Math with IF 0.026-0.034, Math with General 0.045-0.049 (below Math with Think-SFT 0.109 and at the level of the base matrix's own top directions 0.042). Mix overlaps all its ingredients: IF 0.380, Code 3.0 0.306, General 0.244, Math 3.0 0.197. Each release pair is the nearest neighbour of the other (4 of 4), so the reward is readable from the weights across runs. Output-side overlap is 3 to 5 times lower (Math 3.0/3.1 0.098, Math/Code 0.07-0.10). Whole-difference cosines stay under 0.03 except with Mix (IF 0.100, Code 3.0 0.068). Spec predictions: X1 (RL pairs above RL-SFT pairs) holds on average (0.186 vs 0.063) but only 14 of 21 pairs; X2 holds (base matrix 0.037); X3 overlap with Math 3.1 against cue score Spearman 0.77, n 6 (Code 3.0 overlaps 0.218 and gains nothing). Reading: the input side follows the text the run generated (reasoning runs against instruction runs), so the idea-ac4e14 claim 'non-math directions carry the math gain' has no support for IF or General. Stating the answer explains about 0.5 of the 9.9 points between cued base and RL on MATH-500 (T 1.0, mean of 4 samples, n=500): label-free extraction rules (grader v4a = v3 + 5 rules, a grader correction for both models, not a method) turn 10 of the base's 2,000 samples right and 0 of RL's, 0 right-to-wrong: base 1,642 -> 1,652, RL 1,840, gap 9.9 -> 9.4 points (change -0.5 [-0.8, -0.2]); vote over 4 unchanged (446, 474). Gold-aware ceiling: 31 of 2,000 base samples have a gold-equal value in the last 5 lines (finished or no answer) against 5 for RL; 14 of 20 read state the gold, so about 22 samples = 1.1 points at most. The rules as first written (v4) gained +0.8 but accepted 6 wrong answers (5 cap hits with a mid-reasoning 'the answer is X'); amended after reading the flips, so v4a is optimistic. H1 (>= 2 points) refuted. Forced-suffix generation (Part B) not run: no prefix input in run_cell.py yet; eligible 21 base / 0 RL samples, ceiling +0.65 point; exact job in the spec.
